item.title: Paradigms of Generic Programming: Archetype, Ducktype, Subtype
item.description:
Generic Is Not Synonymous with Template

What is generic programming? When people hear “generic programming”, many immediately think of templates, but template programming is only one paradigm of generic programming. Alexander Stepanov, who coined the term “generic programming”, repeatedly emphasized: generic programming is not about how to use templates. The first version of the STL, despite having “template” in its name, was actually implemented on top of Scheme.

To Be Generic, You Need Specifications

Defining specifications and conforming to them is the foundation of generic programming. Any kind of generic programming requires some specification; only with a specification can one abstraction be adapted to multiple concrete entities. Without a specification, the people writing concrete implementations would have no idea what rules to follow, what interfaces to implement, or what conditions to satisfy — and generic programming would naturally be out of the question.
